svg.aria-label: IQ-TREE3-GPU: an alignment of eight bacterial genomes becomes a tree; Felsenstein pruning computes conditional likelihoods up the tree; the same calculation runs on CPU and GPU on the largest benchmark case (65 genomes, 5.12x faster at 20 threads; benchmark medians 1.33x at 20 threads and 6.97x at 1 thread); one NNI move reaches the maximum-likelihood tree.
svg.text: One column, site 2,270, is followed through every stage.
Children before parents, for each of 2,194 site patterns and 4 rate categories.
The largest analysis in the benchmark: speedup grows with tree size and complexity. Medians over all
benchmark datasets: 1.33× at 20 threads (n = 145) and 6.97× at 1 thread (n = 30).
IQ-TREE proposes the move; the GPU evaluates its likelihood.
UFBoot support, 1,000 replicates. The speedup of your own data depends on its size: see When it pays off below.
Example genome set shipped with the tool: examples/data/example_CAG-269.faa
8 gut genomes of the genus CAG-269. Stages 1, 2 and 4 use this alignment; stage 3 uses a large benchmark case.
Each tip = one bacterial genome (MAG); label = host species | MAG ID
conditional likelihood of node v from its children
pruning uses a computational root; the ML tree itself is unrooted
